items.note: Tenney TVAC brochure and product page give no cooldown/pull-down time for the platen. They give only a transition rate ('5°C per minute average over the range of -40°C to -80°C'), and computing a time from it would be an estimate. They also give a vacuum pump-down time ('ultimate vacuum within 6 hours or less'; product page: 5.0 x 10-6 Torr within four hours), which is pumping, not cooling. Vessel size is per order.

items.quote: The cooling phase will take approximately 2 to 3.5 hours depending on the set chamber temperature.
items.document_title: Thermo Scientific CryoStar NX70 Operator Guide
items.note: Initial cool-down after switch-on with default -15 C blade holder/specimen head settings; the upper bound (3.5 h) is used as max.

items.quote: For temperature and humidity equilibration some 20-30 minutes are required (also see test read-outs provided with the instrument).
items.location: User Manual PN 103261 Rev G, General Remarks on the Operational Procedures
items.document_title: Vitrobot Mark IV User Manual PN 103261
items.note: Time for the climate chamber to reach its set temperature/humidity (operating condition, 4-60 C). The cryogen side (LN2 pre-cooling of the coolant container and condensing ethane) is done by the user and the manual gives no time for it, so it is not included.

TSCM48XV Technical Data Sheet Rev-B gives only freezing/warming rates (0.1-99.9 C/min, no load) and no time to reach a set point; the chamber follows the user's freezing profile. Deriving a time from the rate would be an estimate. The CryoMed brochure URL returned a security-verification page (no text).

items.location: TSX Universal Series ULT freezers - Medical Device brochure, page 5, Table A
items.document_title: Thermo Scientific TSX Universal Series ULT freezers - Medical Device brochure
items.note: Table A columns are TSX70086LA, TSX70086A, TSX60086LA, TSX60086A, ...; the third value (287 min, ~5 h) is TSX60086LA, pull-down 20 C to -80 C. Caveat: the brochure footnote states the data is representative performance and 'not published product specifications'.

Thermotron BC-155 brochure and the ATS-320-V model pages give load capacities and '9-point product recovery in 15 minutes or less' (recovery after basket transfer, MIL-STD-883 1010), but no pull-down time from ambient for either zone. Recovery time is not a cooldown time.

Thermotron BC-150 altitude-chamber brochure, the altitude-chamber page and FA-16 model pages give the temperature range (-73 to 177 C), workspace and electrical data, but no temperature pull-down time or rate.

The measurement head sits in an integrated LN2 dewar that the user fills from an LN2 supply (0.5 bar). There is no refrigerator with a cooldown cycle, and the June 2024 datasheet gives no fill or cooldown time.
Same platform as TAPESTAR XL: an integrated LN2 dewar filled by the user from an LN2 supply, with no refrigerator cooldown. The June 2024 XL-HF datasheet gives no fill or cooldown time.

The Tinius Olsen EC2368 datasheet only states 'Heating/cooling time to maximum temperature from ambient typical <80min depending on masses in chamber'. That is time to the maximum (600 C), not cooldown to -150 C with the LN2 Dewar, and no LN2 pull-down time is given on the product page.
Passive 7 L NGD-1030 LN2 dewar with HTS SQUID sensors, filled by the user. There is no refrigerator cooldown; the datasheet gives only the hold time (2-3 weeks) and no fill or cooldown time.

ZwickRoell PI 486 gives a cycle time of ≤1.5 minutes and a feeding time of ≤5 s, which are per-specimen test cycle values. It gives no time for the LN2 tempering unit to cool specimens from ambient to -180 C, and the product page has none either.
